excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
Haven't seen this room before. 

> What do you propose instead?

<@!311971895828283393> geth has extricated account mgmt to `clef`, a CLI tool which has an external interface for signing-requests, and an internal interface, either for the CLI UI or for a custom UI in whatever language /framework people are comfortable with. I'd be happy to add relevant methods to clef to be able to use it for 2.0 aswell

excerpts.author: raulj
excerpts.content: Thanks <@!211091239112671234> , had not heard of this before! shall look into it

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
> The alternative is to ask for manual input of every password for every keystore when the validator client starts up

The clef alternative is to enable scripting instead of 'unlock'. So in place of an actual user, a script can take the seat. It can inspect the signing-request, and approve/deny. If approved (either by a human or a script), then clef checks if it already has the password in it's encrypted db. If it doesn't it asks the UI/human for pw
